title: Boyd Atkins, Heebie Jeebies and criticism of Louis's band
summary: Mason tells how Boyd Atkins wrote Heebie Jeebies, and defends Louis against critics.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: The boy by the name of, uh... Boyd Atkins. Boyd Atkins was playing the violin in the band, you know. And, uh... He left the band and went to Chicago. And, uh... They had a... They had a little paper or something around Chicago called Heba Jeebus. They had to... Used to... Used to have a... Either the paper or... They had some... A little deal. They printed the paper called Heba Jeebus. And this boy wrote the, uh... Wrote this tune called Heba Jeebus. And, of course, uh... Uh... The, uh... The Heba Jeebus had a trumpet solo in the... The back... Down there, a coda, which was quite... Well, it was quite popular. Most tunes at that time had, uh... What they call a coda. Mm-hmm. And they had this coda, which was very, uh... A difficult trumpet... Uh... Trumpet solo there. And, uh... When Van Lewis, uh... Of course, uh... When Van Lewis, uh... Got through with the, uh... Uh... Playing that, uh... That piece at Heba Jeebus... Instead of playing this, uh... This trumpet part there... That was doing the music, he made that scat. That scat, uh... That scat thing on the, uh... On the, uh... On that piece. And, of course, uh... It's history what, uh... What really happened, of course. He... It was an instant... Instantaneous hit. I say... I think, though, for Lewis, as far as Lewis is concerned, I remember when, uh... Before he went to Europe... How all the papers out in the East, He was criticizing all the time. Calling him or talking about him as his one-man band. Of course, we had a fellow here, uh... A fellow from... Our St. Louis that went with Lewis. His name was Z.T. Randolph. That played a trumpet. And did arranging for him. And, uh... Uh... Quite a few people used to have said, uh... Well... Uh... They thought... They thought Lewis didn't have much for the band, Because he, uh... Oh, he didn't... The man only played a few chords, But I found out... The only way for a man to really popularize what he wants to do, When he's good, Is to get his group like that. And, uh... And I'm quite sure... The public, right now, Is being benefited... In the selection... In the choice he made. I remember when he was playing with, uh... Uh... Playing with a band... Coming on stage in... Uh... In Chicago, playing at the, uh... Uh... Theater there, let me see... I... Erskine Tate. He used to come there and play on the stage for Erskine Tate's... You know... Played a tune, you know... And then he went with his band. He was playing, I think, over there... Not a terrace... Uh... They had another nightclub in Chicago at that time... That, uh... Where he played. He and Earl Hines and... Uh... Some of the fellas... I don't remember the name of the nightclub right now... But the thing about it... The one thing that's, uh... That's very, uh... That's very... Is outstanding in... Is that Lewis knew what he wanted to do... And, of course, had he, uh... Had he probably pinned himself down in some band... He never would have gotten a chance to play... Like he wanted. And by sticking out for himself... In spite of the fact he was criticized... He got a chance to put over what he wanted to...
